findings.reason: the plan's §2 write-path list (file_memo, serve, resources, roadmap, fleet_index, _plan_html) omits project_state.py, so the duplicate survived; adding project_state.py to that list and routing both the signature and the cache to `file_memo.memoized("plan_state", path, ...)` is what collapses the two owners into one.
findings.text: `_plan_file_signature` re-implements `file_memo.file_signature` (the identical dev/ino/size/mtime/ctime tuple) and `_cached_plan_state` (line 1191) hand-rolls the stat-keyed memo with its own `_PLAN_STATE_CACHE` and lock (declared line 96), a second cache owner beside the one the plan created; the duplicate is live on the served path through `compose_project_state` → `_cached_plan_state` (line 1228), so a change to the file-identity contract must now be made in two places.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `reckon/file_memo.py` hides stat-identity keying, deep-copy isolation, torn-read protection and LRU eviction behind three calls (`memoized`, `file_signature`, `clear`), and it is now the imported parse owner across thirteen modules; `resource_scan_scope` likewise hides ContextVar scan reuse behind a context manager.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan introduced `file_memo.file_signature` as the stat-identity owner but left `reckon/project_state.py` hand-rolling the same signature and cache on the served path.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan extends existing machinery rather than adding a subsystem beside it: `metadata_index._covered_files` is the one tree walk reused by `_walk_discovery_signature` (reckon/serve.py:1577); `_FleetChangeWatch` reuses `_ProjectChangeWatch.consume()` (reckon/serve.py:299); `resource_scan_scope` is the shared scan reuse wired into `iter_resources` (reckon/resources.py:439); and no equivalent per-file stat memo existed before `file_memo`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `_FleetChangeWatch` extends `_ProjectChangeWatch` by exposing its descriptor read as `consume()` (reckon/serve.py:176,299) rather than adding a parallel watcher, and the `memoized(...)` call sites forward to the shared owner `file_memo`, not to a competing memo; no wrapper in the plan lacks that justification.
